medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
For many years, Katz has been among the top medical schools for enrolling and graduating physicians from a broad range of life experiences. Our current student body represents a wide range of cultural, social and economic backgrounds. As the fabric of society becomes more varied, it is critical that we continue to build on our success. 

The Office of Strategic Partnerships in Health, Education & Resources (SPHERE) sponsors ongoing programs, events and activities designed to support and enrich the educational journey of students as they navigate their career paths. These include: pathway programs for high school and college students as well as a summer pre-matriculation program for medical students.

Mini Med School - exposes high school students to opportunities in healthcare.

Medical and Basic Science Scholars Research Program - faculty introduce college students to the research world.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence is an administrative measure granted at the discretion of the Senior Associate Dean for Medical Education. It is used in situations where it is deemed in the best interest of the student and/or the School that the student's medical education be interrupted.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Katz students at both the North Philadelphia and St. Luke’s Regional Campus are able to participate in a wide range of student organizations and activities. Students can be elected to serve in the Student Government Association, Honor Board, and on a variety of institutional committees. One of Temple’s strengths is the number of community service and volunteer activities available for students. For many students the availability of community service and volunteer experiences is a major reason for selecting Katz and one of the top reasons they recommend the school to potential applicants. Opportunities include: health-based programs, programs in local schools, foundation-funded national service and global health activities. Additionally, other extracurricular enrichment activities provide opportunities for students to engage with peers and faculty advisors in special interest groups, many of which are centered on a specific clinical discipline.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Temple’s Health Sciences Center, home to the Katz North Philadelphia campus, Kornberg School of Dentistry, & the School of Pharmacy, offers a dynamic, collaborative environment for both students & health care professionals.  Temple Health is widely recognized for providing exceptional care to the surrounding community as well as specialized tertiary & quaternary services that draw patients, faculty & students from Philadelphia and beyond.

The St. Luke’s regional campus, located in Bethlehem, PA is associated with the St. Luke's University Health Network - a non-profit, regional, fully integrated, nationally recognized health network providing services in the Lehigh Valley & beyond.

Our newest regional campus will matriculate their first class in fall 2027. WellSpan regional campus located in York, PA is associated with WellSpan Health - an integrated healthcare delivery system that serves 12 counties throughout Central Pennsylvania and Northern Maryland.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Students live in a variety of neighborhoods in the Philadelphia region.  Students who live in neighborhoods about 20 minutes northwest of campus: Roxborough, Manayunk and East Falls require a car to travel to the Health Sciences campus. Students who live downtown: Center City, South Philadelphia, South Street, Italian Market, and the Art Museum neighborhoods take the SEPTA Broad Street line to campus for the preclerkship phase. 

Students at the St. Luke's and WellSpan regional campuses have housing options that include rental apartments, housing sublets and home purchases. Many students live nearby and can walk to campus or drive from local communities. 

A car is needed to travel to clinical learning sites in phase 2 and 3 of the curriculum at all campuses.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
Support for Temple’s sexual and gender minority students begins on interview day when applicants meet a faculty and student member of the LGBTQIA2S+ community at Temple. The LGBTQ and Allies in Medicine student group hosts a welcome event with LGBTQIA2S+ faculty, residents, and students from Temple’s other health professions schools and hosts speakers, social events, and tables at Pride and Outfest. The group is also involved with community organizations such as Washington West Project and the Mazzoni Center.

Temple is the proud sponsor of the annual Philadelphia-wide LGBTQIA2S+ residency forum which brings together students and physicians from around Philadelphia to discuss being LGBTQIA2S+ in medicine and what role being LGBTQIA2S+ might play in the residency application process.

Katz students are engaged in efforts to ensure inclusion of sexual and gender minorities in the curriculum and also conduct research in LGBTQIA2S+ health education.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Office of Disability Resources and Services (DRS) at Temple University has a staff member who works with Katz to provide to students information about types of accommodations, how to apply for them, and to ensure appropriate implementation. Accommodations fall into two categories:  testing and clinical. For testing accommodations, there is a shared roster where the information is stored and updated as necessary.  For clinical accommodations, the student, OSS staff, and clerkship faculty meet prior to the rotation to clarify and develop a communication plan.  A memo with the pertinent information is sent to the appropriate personnel involved with the rotation. Meetings are held between DRS and Katz dean’s staff to review policies, troubleshoot and problem solve when necessary, determine any changes and address concerns. Annually DRS and OSS meet with faculty to present updated DRS information in addition to a Technical Standards review to assess for accuracy and revise if necessary.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Katz supports student well-being in several ways.  A Well-being Advisory Committee, comprised of faculty, students, and staff from departments throughout the medical school, meets monthly to share information, assess student needs, ensure access, and support and implement programming. The Office of Student Support (OSS) collaborates with Temple University’s Tuttleman Counseling Center so that students have access to confidential therapeutic services.  Each student also is assigned an academic coach who meets with students at least twice per year to discuss progress and assist with issues that emerge.  Additional collaborations include: Student Faculty Center, Resilience Resource Center, Disability Resources and Services, the Library, all of which provide resources, events, and activities for students seeking assistance or wanting to tend to their wellness.

Recognizing the importance of building community, Katz encourages strong peer support networks.  This includes OWLs, “Our Wellness Liaisons,” a peer support group that is associated with our Doctoring Colleges / Learning Communities (there are 2 OWLs per college) and work with faculty to organize social events, ensure students have information about resources, and coordinate programming. OWLs also collaborate with OSS on events such as the Katz Resource Fair, supporting the NESTs (a vertical peer linkage from M1 – M4) and “Pop-up Snack Events" where students can mingle.  Peer Academic Facilitators (PAFs) are available for tutoring. The Student Government Association collaborates with the Office of Student Support to implement and support programs and activities that promote and ensure student well-being such as a the bi-annual Talent Show and College Cup Tournaments.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Katz prepares students to lead with purpose—as compassionate clinicians, bold scientists, and community-driven changemakers. Our students come from all walks of life, united by a shared calling to improve community health. Whether you’re a recent college graduate, a career changer, or someone driven by lived experience, you’ll find your place at Katz. Within our non-competitive, collegial environment, students will have access to high-touch advising and academic coaches that will help students reach their potential.  Clinical experiences are truly hands-on, giving students the skills needed to excel in residency and beyond.

Our students are highly engaged in our local community and driven to improve the health of marginalized communities. They work with community-based organizations and learn how to advocate for their communities. Katz is where rigorous education meets real-world impact and where you’ll gain the skills to lead in patient care, education, science, and service.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Proper attire, including a white coat, should be worn for all patient encounters, events occurring in healthcare settings, and activities involving simulated patients or patient instructors.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Course directors, faculty & deans are available to meet students’ needs. The Office of Student Support oversees academic coaching, peer tutoring, personal counseling/wellness & career advising.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students work with standardized & actual patients beginning in their first year Doctoring course. Students participate in the care of patients in all required Phase 2 & 3 courses & clinical electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Large group didactic sessions, case-based discussions, clinical reasoning conferences, point of care ultrasound workshops & experiential learning sessions taught in the sim center & clinical settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Phase 2 clerkships & electives begin in spring of the second calendar year. Phase 3 consists of electives & required clinical courses including a sub-internship, intensive care & emergency medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: The PREP program supports students’ transition to medical school by providing early exposure to the curriculum and fostering effective study skills to navigate the rigor of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Small group learning & Doctoring activities required.  Large group, didactic sessions are presented in person, live streamed & recorded for students to learn at their own pace or review independently.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Our competency-based curriculum provides the opportunity to learn, practice & apply the scientific knowledge, clinical skills and professional attributes/behaviors essential to the practice of medicine. Phase 1 is organized in Fundamentals and Systems courses that integrate basic and clinical sciences in the presentation of normal structure and function, pathophysiology and disease, diagnostic strategies, and patient management. In the Doctoring courses, students apply learning from the Fundamentals and Systems courses while learning and practicing patient interviewing skills, physical exam maneuvers, clinical reasoning and communication skills and engage in interactive sessions focused on critical topics that affect the health and well-being of patients and communities and promote patient-centered care (e.g. the social determinants of health, bias and structural racism and patient safety and quality improvement).

During Phase 2, students complete a variety of core clerkships. Intersession courses before each block prepare students to participate as a member of the patient care team on day one of the upcoming clinical rotations. Elective courses in this phase allow students to explore a variety of medical specialties.

During Phase 3, students complete required and elective courses that allow them to assume advanced patient care responsibilities under supervision as members of teams caring for undifferentiated patients in the emergency room, treating severe illnesses in critical care units and as sub-interns. Students complete a Faculty Mentored Scholarly Experience during which they engage in scholarly work with a faculty advisor in an area of interest: Health outcomes and clinical research, basic and translational science research, scholarship in quality improvement, educational scholarship, scholarly evaluation of a community engagement or global health project or scholarly evaluation of an intervention to promote diversity, equity and inclusion.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
Medical students are exposed to primary care medicine in the longitudinal Doctoring course in the preclerkship phase and in required clerkships in Family Medicine, Pediatrics and Internal Medicine in the clerkship phase of the curriculum. Clinical elective rotations in primary care specialties are available in Phase 3 of the curriculum.

Over the last several years, approximately 39% of graduates from the School of Medicine have entered residencies in the primary care specialties of pediatrics, family medicine and internal medicine. Learning opportunities in a broad variety of clinical settings prepare graduating students for careers in primary care and in specialty disciplines.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Students learn about research methodology in the MD program and are prepared to engage in research elective experiences available in each phase of the curriculum. Learning about and participating in research is important to nurture a spirit of inquiry and to generate new knowledge that contributes to the health of patients and communities. Students can participate in research activities the summer after first year.

Biomedical research is conducted collaboratively within the school's basic science and clinical departments and research centers. Among the many opportunities, strengths reside in the research areas of Alzheimer's disease, cardiovascular disease, neuroscience, metabolic disease, substance use disorder, lung disease, cancer biology, HIV, and translational medicine. Collaborative investigations among clinical, basic and translational research units provides a rich environment for increasing knowledge to improve health outcomes.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Our student-centered philosophy & relationships with outstanding faculty with a passion for teaching fosters a collegial learning environment. Academic coaches support students’ progress and success.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community service and service learning are offered throughout the curriculum. In Phase 1, a service learning elective and a summer regional community health service learning program are available.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students complete research projects in the Faculty Mentored Scholarly Experience course.  Research electives are available during each curricular phase and during the summer between 1st and 2nd year.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Temple Health; St Luke's University Health Network; WellSpan Health; Lancaster General Hospital; St Christopher's Hospital for Children; Main Line Health Network, Chestnut Hill Hospital.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Phase 1 courses including Doctoring:  Pass, Fail

Phase 2 and 3 (clerkship/post-clerkship):  Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail or Pass, Fail

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Founded in 1901 as Pennsylvania’s first co-educational medical school, the Lewis Katz School of Medicine has attained a national reputation for training humanistic clinicians and biomedical scientists. The school attracts students and faculty committed to making a difference in patient care, research, education & public service at home and across the globe.

The MD program is completed at the North Philadelphia, St. Luke’s regional campus, or WellSpan regional campus. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in basic science and clinical medicine and enables students to acquire the knowledge, clinical and lifelong learning skills, and professional attributes needed to meet the needs of diverse patient populations. 

Students gain experience in a variety of urban, suburban, and rural in- and out-patient locations. They learn to provide culturally competent, interprofessional care to a diverse population of patients with simple conditions as well as highly complex cases.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission
Align with our diverse communities to advance medicine and improve health through education, research, training, and development of the next generation of clinicians, educators, and scientists.

Vision
The Lewis Katz School of Medicine will inspire a new standard of excellence in education and research and lead social change in medicine.

At the Katz School of Medicine, our mission and vision call us to serve, discover, and lead. We believe medicine is not only a science but also a promise. A promise to our patients, our communities, and to the next generation of healers and innovators. Together, we create a future where knowledge, compassion, and collaboration improve lives everywhere.

In 2024, the school launched Inspiring Excellence, a five-year strategic plan that charts a big and bold future that harnesses the unlimited potential and passion deeply embedded within the community and honors a long history of valuing and embracing diversity and health equity. Inspiring Excellence reflects Katz’s commitment to shaping the future of health. It centers on aligning with our communities, advancing equity, and raising the bar in medical education and research. Together, these priorities create a powerful framework for lasting social change in medicine.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: Washington & Jefferson College in Washington, PA
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The Medical Scholars Program provides an opportunity for exceptionally qualified high school seniors to gain a conditional acceptance to LKSOM upon completion of their undergraduate degree. Applicants to the BA/MD program must first be accepted to Washington & Jefferson College. Candidates who meet specific criteria are recommended to the School of Medicine for an interview.

Students with  strong academic background who have completed a variety of AP coursework and demonstrated exceptional standardized test performance are eligible for the program. A minimum SAT score of 1350, with no section less than 600 or a minimum ACT composite score of 31 is required. Students with demonstrated leadership and extensive community and health care experience are encouraged to apply.

Matriculation to LKSOM is conditional upon successful completion of all program requirements.

The deadline and restrictions listed below are for students who are completing the BA/MD program and applying to Katz.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: AAMC Certiphi Background Check, PA Child Abuse Check, FBI fingerprint check
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Katz considers letters of recommendation from a premedical committee, a packet from a school letter compilation service, or between three (3) and six (6) individual letters.  If submitting a compilation packet or individual letters, we prefer if possible, but do not require two (2) letters from professors with whom you have completed course work from the AMCAS course classifications of Biology, Chemistry, or Physics.  
* One (1) additional letter is recommended from a non-science professor, work experience, or service activity
* A premedical committee letter does not need a specific number of science/non-science letters
* We welcome letters from research experiences, but prefer them in addition to the requested science letters from professors with whom you completed coursework
* At any point in the application process, you are welcome to submit additional letters to support your application and are encouraged to use the AMCAS letter service to submit these letters
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
The interview day includes a welcome from an admissions office representative who provides an overview of the admissions process, medical curriculum, as well as the clinical, service learning and extracurricular opportunities. 

Candidates interviewing at each campus participate in three interviews. A primary interview with a physician or PhD faculty member who is on the Admissions Committee, a secondary/blind interview with a faculty member or a student member of the admissions committee who is blinded to the application materials, and a community interview with a member of the local community.

The interview day also includes a virtual tour of the campus and an information session with current medical students where the applicant will be able to learn more about student life.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Applicants have 3 interviews. A Primary Interview with a faculty member of the Admissions Committee, a Second Interview with a faculty member or a student member of the admissions committee, and an Interview with a member of the local community.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Candidates being considered for admission to the St. Luke’s or WellSpan Health regional campuses will interview with faculty from the regional campus.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: At this time, Katz plans to conduct all interviews in a virtual format for applicants in the 2027 application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: After receipt of a verified AMCAS® application, an email is sent to US citizens or those with permanent resident or refugee/asylee status with a link to the online supplemental application.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: AMCAS application and transcript deadline is 8/1.  Supplemental application and letter deadline is 8/15. Applicants selected for interview will interview in September with decision prior to 10/1.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Temple considers applications from U.S. citizens or those with permanent resident or refugee/asylee status with the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
After receipt of a verified application from AMCAS ®, an automated email from the Office of Admissions is sent to candidates with details about how to access the Katz online supplemental application. 

MCAT®
The supplemental application can be submitted prior to receipt of MCAT® scores. Complete applications will be reviewed after the 2026 MCAT® scores are received. Applications are considered using the most recent MCAT® results (section scores and total scores). 

Coursework
Applicants should demonstrate preparation for the rigors of medical school and achievement in the sciences through completion of a broad range of science coursework and the MCAT® exam. While there are no absolute course requirements, Katz recommends that students complete coursework in Biology, Chemistry (both general and organic), Biochemistry, Physics, Psychology and Sociology. In addition, students should have a broad humanities education and strong writing skills. The Office of Admissions will only evaluate courses completed at a US or Canadian university. 

If recommended coursework in Biology, Chemistry or Physics has been completed using AP credits, online, at a community college, or through a study abroad program, we prefer to see classroom-based, upper-level science coursework in that discipline.

Coursework completed online or with P/F grades due to COVID will not negatively impact the review of your application.

Grading
For the spring 2020 semester, many schools offered the option for Pass/Fail in lieu of a letter grade. This will not impact the review of a candidate’s application.

Other
All applicants to the MD program are required to complete Casper, an online open-response situational judgement test (SJT). Casper is a scenario-based test that assesses non-cognitive skills and interpersonal characteristics that we believe are important for success in our program and complements the other tools that we use for applicant screening and selection.

An individualized holistic review of each complete application including, but not limited to, the candidate's academic history, the college attended, MCAT® scores, Casper results, recommendations, extracurricular activities, work experience, medically-related experience, and community service activities is used to select candidates for interview. While not required, many students have participated in research activities and this information is also considered.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee considers all MCAT® scores but places the greatest emphasis on the applicants most recent MCAT® score.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: If recommended coursework in Biology, Chemistry or Physics has been completed at a community college, we prefer to see classroom-based, upper-level science coursework in that discipline.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants may submit letters of intent, letters of interest, and notice of significant updates or achievements by uploading directly to the Katz online application portal.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Applicants affirm that they can meet the LKSOM technical standards for the MD degree, with or without accommodations, on the supplemental application. Prior to matriculation, accepted students are required to attest, in writing, that they can meet the LKSOM Technical Standards fpr the MD degree, with or without accommodations.  Enrolled students must attest, in writing, that they meet the standards with or without accommodations prior to entry into phase 2 and before entry into phase 3 of the curriculum.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Office of Student Financial Services works with students during their medical school career to provide information on current funding sources, as well as debt management counseling to help plan for their financial future. A thorough, structured program of financial counseling and debt management is offered throughout the four years of medical school. 

There are a variety of funding sources available to students, which include outside scholarships, low-interest rate loans, as well as scholarships and grants established by the Office of Institutional Advancement, friends of the University and other state/local entities. All accepted students who complete an electronic institutional application are considered for scholarships. Accepted students are notified of institutional scholarships starting in March through matriculation.

Students are encouraged to complete a FAFSA by March 1 prior to matriculation. 

Tuition is approved annually by Temple University’s Board of Trustees. Current tuition and fees can be found here: https://bursar.temple.edu/sites/bursar/files/Tuition_Rates.pdf
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: The tuition at the medical school is set by the University Board of Trustees.  The percentage increase is generally the same across all schools and colleges at the University.

medSchoolSpecialty.specialtyTrainingTxt: The Katz Career Advising Program is an integrated, longitudinal program designed to support career exploration, elective selection and career decision-making for all medical students at the North Philadelphia and regional campuses.  Throughout the students’ enrollment, the Offices of Undergraduate Medical Education and Student Support provide specific individual advising related to elective selection and career decision-making.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Katz offers several early assurance programs that allow students to be considered for acceptance in their junior year of college. Early Assurance candidates from Temple University and Washington & Jefferson College are able to complete the MD program at the North Philadelphia, St. Luke’s regional campus, or WellSpan regional campus. The St. Luke’s and WellSpan regional campus each have an Early Assurance program for students from local colleges. Students interested in the Early Assurance Program are nominated by their pre-medical advisor.

Katz offers the Advanced Core in Medical Sciences (ACMS) postbaccalaureate program that is designed for those who have completed their foundational science (pre-med) coursework in their undergraduate program and have demonstrated a passion for medicine and service.. Acceptance to the ACMS program includes a conditional acceptance to Katz.

Matriculation from all linkage programs is conditional upon successful completion of all program requirements.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The MD/MA in Health Justice and Bioethics offers Katz students an integrated program focused on health equity in clinical care, research, and policy. Housed in Temple’s Center for Health Justice and Bioethics, the program trains students to examine ethical challenges facing structurally marginalized communities, where social and institutional inequities shape health outcomes. Coursework combines theoretical and applied bioethics with methodological tools for ethical analysis, policy evaluation, advocacy, and community engagement. Designed to align with the MD curriculum, the MA can be completed concurrently without extending medical school training.

Students can also complete an online MD/MBA (offered through the Fox School of Business) or a MD/Graduate Certificate in Narrative Medicine.  No additional time is required to complete the MBA or Certificate in Narrative Medicine.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: All applicants to the MD program are required to complete Casper, an online open-response situational judgement test (SJT). Casper is a scenario-based test that assesses non-cognitive skills and interpersonal characteristics that we believe are important for success in our program and complements the other tools that we use for applicant screening and selection. Casper tests are valid for one admissions cycle. For entering 2027, Casper test dates March 19, 2026 to January 5, 2027 are considered.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Review of the continuing candidate list begins in May and continues until Transition to Medical School. Applicants with a strong interest in Temple are encouraged to send updates starting in April.
